DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Thesis [L4].** Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human male as the source of his begetting. Joseph was his legal and reputed father, not his biological one. By "biological father" I mean a man whose begetting supplies the child. The KJV text answers that question on six rows.

---

## 1. Matthew's genealogy changes its verb and its pronoun at the end

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat, fathered"), and it is repeated for each father. At the last link, Matthew 1:16 changes to ἐγεννήθη (egennēthē, "was born"), a passive form. The relative pronoun is ἧς (hēs, "of whom"), and it is feminine singular. It can refer only to Mary, not to Joseph. Joseph is called ἀνήρ (anēr, "husband"), not the one who begat.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2 shows the pattern of father begetting son. Matthew 1:16 departs from it by naming the mother as the one "of whom" Jesus was born.

**[L4]** From the pattern in Matthew 1:2, the change of verb in 1:16 [L2], and the feminine "of whom" [L2], the genealogy ends on Mary as the source of the birth and Joseph as the husband. The text turns on the very line where a father's begetting would otherwise appear.

---

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and it came before the couple came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** In 1:18, συνελθεῖν (synelthein, "to come together," here used of marital union) fixes the pregnancy before any union. In 1:18 and 1:20 the source is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Spirit"); ἐκ (ek) marks origin. In 1:20, "conceived" is γεννηθέν (gennēthen), the passive of the same verb rendered "begat" in Matthew 1:2. The text assigns to the Holy Ghost, not to a man, the origin of what is begotten in her.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The word ἐγίνωσκεν (eginōsken, "knew," used of marital knowledge) is negated up to the birth.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the union [L2: synelthein]. Matthew 1:20 names the origin of the conception as ek pneumatos hagiou [L2]. Matthew 1:25 confirms no union up to the birth [L3]. So no man's begetting lies behind the conception.

---

## 3. Mary herself rules out a man, and the angel names the cause

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** In 1:34, γινώσκω (ginōskō, "I know," used of marital knowledge) is joined with ἄνδρα (andra, "a man, a male"). In 1:35, the Holy Ghost ἐπελεύσεται (epeleusetai, "shall come upon") and the power ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei, "shall overshadow"). The conjunction διό (dio, "therefore, for which reason") ties the title to that cause.

**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." The conceiving is placed in her womb.

**[L4]** Luke 1:34 gives the question, and Luke 1:35 answers it with the coming of the Holy Ghost, not with a man. The "therefore" [L2: dio] makes the Holy Ghost conception the stated reason for the title. A human father's contribution would be an addition the answer in 1:35 never makes, and 1:34 has just excluded it.

---

## 4. The sign is a virgin who conceives

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet... Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

**[L2]** The Hebrew word behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is עַלְמָה (ʿalmāh, H5959), which the KJV renders "virgin" in this verse. Matthew 1:23 uses παρθένος (parthenos, "virgin"). Matthew 1:22 declares the birth the fulfilment, with ἵνα πληρωθῇ (hina plērōthē, "that it might be fulfilled").

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 ("before they came together") shows the condition that fulfils the sign.

**[L4]** The KJV's own wording in Isaiah 7:14 [L1] and its fulfilment in Matthew 1:22–23 [L1 with L2: hina plērōthē] make the sign a virgin who conceives. A biological father would void the sign.

---

## 5. Joseph's fatherhood is "supposed," not stated as begetting

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

**[L2]** In Luke 3:23, ἐνομίζετο (enomizeto, "was reckoned, was supposed by opinion") marks the sonship to Joseph as a view held, not as begetting.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man... was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:20 then gives the angel's instruction to take Mary.

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 [L1] with enomizeto [L2] puts Joseph's sonship as supposed. Luke 2:48 uses "father" in Mary's ordinary speech, and in Luke 2:49 the child's reply names a different Father. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph, before the angel's word, taking the pregnancy as a ground for putting her away. That is not how a man acts who knows himself the cause, and Matthew 1:20 then corrects him by naming the Holy Ghost.

---

## 6. A body was prepared

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** κατηρτίσω (katērtisō, "thou hast prepared, fitted") has God as the one who fitted the body.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." This names the same divine agency in the conception.

**[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 [L1, with L2: katērtisō] and Luke 1:35 [L3] both name God as the one who produced the body, so a human father's begetting is not the source.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew's genealogy ends differently: it changes from egennēsen "begat" (Matthew 1:2) to egennēthē "was born" with the feminine "of whom" (Matthew 1:16, hēs), naming Mary, not Joseph, as the one of whom Jesus was born.
2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18, 1:20; ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Spirit") and was found "before they came together" (synelthein, "to come together"), with the same verb gennēthen "begotten" as in 1:2, supported by Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till."
3. Mary said "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34; ginōskō with andra), and the angel gave the Holy Ghost's coming (Luke 1:35; epeleusetai, episkiasei) as the cause, tied by dio "therefore."
4. The sign was a virgin conceiving (Isaiah 7:14, H5959 rendered "virgin"; Matthew 1:23, parthenos "virgin"; Matthew 1:22, hina plērōthē "that it might be fulfilled").
5. Joseph was "supposed" to be the father (Luke 3:23, enomizeto "reckoned by opinion"), and Matthew 1:19–20 shows him unaware of any begetting of his own until the angel's word; Hebrews 10:5 (katērtisō "prepared") and Luke 1:35 name God as the source of the body.
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father: his conception in Mary was of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph was husband and reputed father only.

# ROUND 2: Christ had no biological father

## ANSWER TO THE QUESTION PUT: how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"?

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**[L2]** "Evident" is πρόδηλος (prodēlos, G4271, "plain before all men, obvious"). "Sprang" is ἀνατέλλω (anatellō, G393, "to rise, spring up"). Together the words state that the tribe he rose from lay open to all.

**[L3]** The open ground the text gives is the house. Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David." This gives Joseph's house, and I grant it. The text reckons sons into a house by taking and naming:
- Exodus 2:10: "he became her son."
- Esther 2:7: "whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter."
- Ezra 2:61: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."
- Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."

**[L4]** The angel addresses Joseph as "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20) and commands him to take Mary and name the child. By Exodus 2:10, Esther 2:7 and Ezra 2:61, taking and naming place a child in a man's house and name. So Hebrews 7:14 and Numbers 1:18 are answered through Joseph's house by legal placing. The flesh descent is stated separately, at Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 (see C1 below).

---

## ANSWERS TO THE CHALLENGER'S CHAIN

**C1. "Seed," "loins," "bowels."**

- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ." Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:9: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham." The "father" of 7:10 is Abraham, a remote ancestor.
- **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751, "loin; procreative power") is used in Hebrews 7:10 of descent through generations. Luke 1:32 likewise calls David "his father David," a king long dead.
- **[L4]** In the very verses cited, "loins" and "father" are used of remote ancestors (Hebrews 7:9–10; Luke 1:32). So Acts 2:30 carries descent from David and does not turn on the immediate father's begetting.
- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]** "Made" is γίνομαι (ginomai, G1096, "to come to be, be made"), not a verb of begetting.
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." This is the same verb with the woman as the stated source. Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."
- **[L3]** Genesis 25:23 says of Rebekah: "two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels." The word behind 2 Samuel 7:12's "bowels" is *meʿeh* (H4578), and it is used of a woman there.
- **[L4]** The oath's words "bowels" and "body" are used of a mother (Genesis 25:23). The verb is "made" (Romans 1:3), and its parallel is "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4). So the oath's flesh descent is carried by the woman's conceiving, and a father's seed is not required.

**C2. Elisabeth.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth." Luke 1:5: "of the daughters of Aaron."
- **[L3]** Exodus 6:23: "Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife." Numbers 2:3: "Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah."
- **[L4]** Exodus 6:23 states that Aaron took a wife who was the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Naashon. Numbers 2:3 makes Amminadab's son captain of Judah. So the text itself shows Aaron's line joined to Judah, and Luke 1:36's "cousin" of a daughter of Aaron (Luke 1:5) fits a kinship running through Judah's house. Elisabeth's Aaronic descent therefore does not decide which house Mary came from.

**C3. The four voices.**

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** "Supposed" is νομίζω (nomizō, G3543, "to reckon, to hold by opinion"). Luke uses it of a mistake at Luke 2:44: "supposing him to have been in the company." So does Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead," when Paul lived. In Luke 3:23 the parenthesis is the evangelist's own marking of the reckoning as supposition.
- **[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" The speakers are doubters of his origin. Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's."
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23 with the sense of *nomizō* at Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19 makes "father" for Joseph a reckoning. The child's reply at Luke 2:49 names the other Father. So C3's four voices carry reputation, not begetting.

**C4. A union within the marriage.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L2]** "Conceived" in 1:20 is γεννηθέν (gennēthen, "begotten," per the 1611 margin). It is a completed passive: the child was already begotten when the angel spoke to Joseph, before he took her at 1:24.
- **[L4]** By 1:18 and 1:20, the child was already conceived before Joseph took her (1:24). By 1:25, he knew her not until the birth. Genesis 4:1 puts the knowing before the conceiving: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." Matthew's order is the reverse: the conception is already present and the knowing is withheld until the birth. So the challenger's union within the marriage has no place in which to beget.

---

## ANSWERS TO THE PRESSES

**D1 (Matthew 1:16).**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." Genesis 4:25 states the husband's act: "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son."
- **[L4]** Genesis 4:25 names the husband's act. Matthew 1:16 gives the begetting at the Jacob-to-Joseph step ("begat"). Then it names the woman by the feminine "of whom" with a passive "was born," and Joseph by *anēr* ("husband"). Matthew 1:18–20 supplies the cause of the birth, the Holy Ghost. So D1 fits the shift of verb with the stated cause.

**D2 (ek with God).**

- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L2]** In John 1:13, *ek theou* ("out of God") is set against *ek thelēmatos andros* ("out of the will of man").
- **[L4]** From John 1:13, "of God" is set over against "of the will of man" as the origin of the birth. So the same *ek* with the Holy Ghost in Matthew 1:20 is not a covenant label laid over a man's begetting. Matthew 1:20's "for" gives the Holy Ghost as the reason Joseph need not fear.

**D3 (Luke 1:34–35).**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." Luke 1:34 asks about that conceiving: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** The words are *epeleusetai* (G1904, "shall come upon") and *episkiasei* (G1982, "shall overshadow"). Both are future. *Dio kai* means "therefore also."
- **[L4]** The question "How shall this be" in 1:34 refers to the conceiving of 1:31. Verse 35 answers with the future Holy Ghost coming upon her, and then states a consequence with "therefore also." The title is given as the result of the Holy Ghost's coming. The answer to "how" is the Holy Ghost, not a man.
- **Press 1 Chronicles 28:6.** I grant that the title "my son" is given of Solomon with David as father. But in 1 Chronicles 28:6 the title rests on a choice ("I have chosen him [to be] my son"). In Luke 1:35 the title rests on a conception ("that holy thing which shall be born of thee"). The footings differ, so the Solomon row does not fit.

**D4 (Isaiah 7:14).**

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:11: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God; ask [it] either in the depth, or in the height above." Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:3: "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz."
- **[L2]** *ʿalmāh* (H5959) is Rebekah's word in Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." Genesis 24:16 says of her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
- **[L4]** Isaiah 7:11 offers the king a sign from depth or height. That is a wonder, and a child born after a man "approached" (Isaiah 8:3) is an ordinary birth. Isaiah 8:3's child is named Mahershalalhashbaz, not Immanuel. The KJV renders this very word "virgin" in Genesis 24:43, of a woman "neither had any man known her." The 1611 margin for 7:14 keeps "O virgin."

**D5 (Matthew 1:19; Luke 3:23; Hebrews 10:5).**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** "Make a publick example" is παραδειγματίζω (paradeigmatizō, G3856, "to make a public example of" a wrong). "Put away" is ἀπολύω (apolyō, "to release, divorce").
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."
- **[L4]** The press says justness and mercy are Joseph's stated grounds. I agree, and the verse states more. A "public example" (G3856) is made of a wrong done, and Deuteronomy 22:24 judges the wrong of the man who humbled the wife. Joseph's mercy has an object only if he reads the pregnancy as the act of another. A man who knows himself the cause has no wrong to expose. Then 1:20's "for" gives the Holy Ghost as the answer to that fear.
- **[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- **[L2]** "Prepared" is καταρτίζω (katartizō, "to fit, frame"). The speaker says "thou hast prepared me," so God is the one who fitted the body and the body is what was fitted.
- **[L3]** Hebrews 11:3: "the worlds were framed by the word of God." The same verb there carries God's own act as the framer. 1 Corinthians 15:38: "But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him." Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- **[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 names God as the one who fitted the body [L1, L2]. Hebrews 11:3 shows the same verb carrying God's own framing [L3]. 1 Corinthians 15:38 says God gives each body "as it hath pleased him," so the body's form rests on his pleasure [L3]. Luke 1:35 names the Holy Ghost's coming as the cause of "that holy thing" born of Mary [L3]. So the text states God, acting through the Holy Ghost's coming, as the source of this body.

---

## CONCLUSION

**[L4]** The Davidic house and the legal sonship come through Joseph by taking and naming (Matthew 1:20, 1:21, 1:25; Luke 2:4; Exodus 2:10; Esther 2:7). The flesh seed comes "made of a woman" (Romans 1:3; Galatians 4:4; Luke 1:31). The conception was already complete before the taking (Matthew 1:18, 1:20, 1:24), and Matthew 1:25 withholds the knowing until the birth. The cause is stated as the Holy Ghost coming upon her (Luke 1:35), and the sign is a virgin (Isaiah 7:14 with Genesis 24:43). Therefore Christ had no biological father. Joseph was husband and reputed father (Luke 3:23).

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 6 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED**

*Footing for the link: the conception in Mary is of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph is husband and reputed father.*

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;"
- **[L2]** The verb is *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate). It is active, "begat," at each step of the chain in Matthew 1:2 and again at Joseph in 1:16. For Jesus the text changes to "was born," and it places him after "Mary, of whom."
- **[L4]** The chain of begetting ends with "Jacob begat Joseph." Jesus is then "born" of the woman named just before him. That is the chain from Matthew 1:2 [L3] and Matthew 1:16 [L1] to the premise.
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

*Footing for Mary's house.* The premise stands on four rows.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32 is spoken to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35 gives the child as "born of thee."
- **[L2]** *Sperma* (G4690) is "seed... by implication, offspring."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The flesh descent is offspring of David, and the one the child is born of is Mary.
- **[L4]** From Luke 1:32 and 1:35 to Romans 1:3, the flesh descent reaches the child through the one of whom he was born.

*Answer to each pressed witness:*

- **Romans 1:3**, "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The press means "a male seed passed down from David."
  - **[L2]** *Sperma* is glossed "seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring." The gloss carries "offspring" as well.
  - **[L2]** The verb is *ginomai* (G1096, to become, be made), not "begat."
  - **[L3]** Romans 1:3 reads "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ... which was made." Galatians 4:4 reads "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The Son is already the Son who is "made."
  - **[L4]** "Offspring of David" is met by descent through the one he was born of. The text does not call Joseph the begetter anywhere in this verse.
- **Acts 2:30**, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ." The press means "from David's procreative power."
  - **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751) is the loin, internally "procreative power."
  - **[L3]** Luke 1:32 calls David "his father David" of a child whose conception is by the Holy Ghost (Luke 1:35). So "father" is said of a forefather generations back.
  - **[L4]** David's loins are the source of the fruit across the generations ("when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers," 2 Samuel 7:12). The word does not fix that Joseph is the step that begot.
- **Hebrews 7:10**, "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
  - **[L3]** Hebrews 7:9 reads "Levi... payed tithes in Abraham." Both rows speak of a forefather, as Luke 1:32 [L3] speaks of "his father David."
  - **[L4]** The loins name the forefather as the source of the line, so they fit descent through David down to the child.
- **2 Samuel 7:12**, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
  - **[L2]** *Mēʿeh* (H4578) is glossed "the uterus (or of men, the seat of generation)," with "the uterus" listed first.
  - **[L3]** Genesis 25:23 reads "separated from thy bowels," spoken to Rebekah.
  - **[L4]** The word is carried by both sexes in the record. So "proceed out of thy bowels" does not by itself fix a man at each step.
- **Hebrews 7:14**, "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The press means "the tribe was plain to all by pedigree."
  - **[L2]** *Anatellō* (G393) is "to (cause to) arise... spring (up)." *Phylē* (G5443) is "an offshoot, i.e. race or clan."
  - **[L3]** Luke 2:4 reads "he was of the house and lineage of David." Joseph's house was the one publicly reckoned, and the child is reckoned in it by taking and naming. Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
  - **[L3]** Exodus 2:10: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses."
  - **[L4]** What is "plain before all men" [L2] is the house the child stands in, by taking and naming [L3]. That holds without Joseph's begetting.
- **Numbers 1:18**, "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
  - **[L2]** *Bayith* (H1004) is "a house... especially family."
  - **[L3]** Exodus 2:10 shows a son entering a house by taking and naming.
